questions.q:
$\dfrac{x}{x + 4}$ is the ratio of energies of photons produced due to transition of an electron of hydrogen atom from its

(i) third permitted energy level to the second level and

(ii) the highest permitted energy level to the second permitted level.

The value of $x$ will be
questions.solution:
Energy of a photon released in transition of electron in hydrogen atom is given by,

$E = 13 . 6\left(\dfrac{1}{{{n}_{2}}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{{n}_{1}}^{2}}\right)eV$

$⇒ \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{13 . 6\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right)}{13 . 6\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)} = \dfrac{x}{x + 4} ⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}}{\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{x}{x + 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{9} = \dfrac{x}{x + 4}$

$⇒ 5x + 20 = 9x$

$⇒ x = 5$

questions.q: A light of energy $12 . 75eV$ is incident on a hydrogen atom in its ground state. The atom absorbs the radiation and reaches to one of its excited states. The angular momentum of the atom in the excited state is $\dfrac{x}{\pi} \times {10}^{- 17}eVs$. The value of $x$ is ______ (use $h = 4 . 14 \times {10}^{– 15}eVs, c = 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{– 1}$)
questions.solution:
Let the electron jumped to ${n}^{th}$ excited state.

In the ground state, energy $E = - 13 . 6eV$

So, using relation $12 . 75 = 13 . 6\left[\dfrac{1}{{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ 0 . 9375 = \left[1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right] ⇒ {n}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ n = \sqrt{16} = 4$

Now, angular momentum, $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{4h}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2h}{\pi}$

$= \dfrac{2}{\pi} \times 4 . 14 \times {10}^{- 15}$

$= \dfrac{828 \times {10}^{- 17}}{\pi}eVs$

Hence, the value of $x = 828$.

questions.q: In Bohr's atomic model, the electron is assumed to revolve in a circular orbit of radius $0 . 5\overset{∘}{A} .$ If the speed of electron is $2 . 2 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1} .$ Then the current associated with the electron will be__________ $\times {10}^{- 2}mA .$ [Take $\pi$ as $\left\dfrac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.solution:
Time taken to revolve in circular orbit is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pir}{v} = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 11}}{2 . 2 \times {10}^{6}} = \dfrac{10}{7} \times {10}^{- 16}s$

Now, current associated with the electron is $I = \dfrac{e}{T} = \dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{\dfrac{10}{7} \times {10}^{- 16}} = 1 . 12 \times {10}^{- 3}A$
$⇒ I = 1 . 12mA$
Hence, the current is $112 \times {10}^{2}mA$.

questions.q:
Two lighter nuclei combine to form a comparatively heavier nucleus by the relation given below:

$X 12 + X 12 = Y 24$

The binding energies per nucleon $X 12$ and $Y 24$ are $1 . 1MeV$ and $7 . 6MeV$ respectively. The energy released in this process is_____ $MeV$.
questions.solution:
Energy released in the given process $=$ Binding energy of product $-$ Binding energy of reactants.

$= 7 . 6 \times 4 - \left(1 . 1 \times 2\right) \times 2$

$= 30 . 4 - 4 . 4$

$= 26MeV$

questions.q:
A common example of alpha decay is

$23892U{\to}^{234}90Th{+}_{2}{He}^{4} + Q$

Given:

${}^{238}92U = 238 . 05060u$

${}^{234}90Th = 234 . 04360u$

${}^{4}2He = 4 . 00260u$ and $1u = 931 . 5\dfrac{MeV}{{c}^{2}}$

The energy released $\left(Q\right)$ during the alpha decay of ${}^{238}92U$ is _____ $MeV$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the Q-value of the given nuclear reaction can be written as

$Q = \left({m}_{U} - {m}_{Th} - {m}_{He}\right){c}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required Q-value for the reaction.

$\begin{cases}Q & = & \left(238 . 05060u - 234 . 04360u - 4 . 00260u\right){c}^{2} \\ & = & 0 . 0044{c}^{2} \times 931 . 5MeV / {c}^{2} \\ & \approx & 4MeV\end{cases}$
